items.headline: Iran and the U.S. broaden tanker and shipping attacks as Brent breaks USD 100
items.summary: Reuters reports the largest declared wave of reciprocal attacks on shipping since the war began: the U.S. said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers, while Iran said it struck two U.S. vessels and eight tankers near Hormuz. Brent moved above USD 100 and visible vessel traffic through the strait remained severely constrained.
items.whyItMatters: The risk has progressed from infrastructure damage to sustained impairment of maritime energy logistics. This raises the probability of a persistent oil, diesel, freight and inflation shock rather than a short-lived geopolitical premium.
items.agciSignal: CONFIRMED MARITIME ESCALATION / BRENT >100 / ENERGY-INFLATION TAIL RISK UP

items.headline: Greed cools to 75 while Valuation rises to 86; PRICE_DISCIPLINE remains active
items.summary: The AGCI live engine reads Greed 75/100 and Valuation 86/100, with the regime still Correction and the matrix condition PRICE_DISCIPLINE — Wait / Price discipline.
items.whyItMatters: Sentiment is less stretched, but valuation is more extreme. The combination of elevated oil, inflation risk and rich multiples argues for better entry prices rather than broad beta expansion.
items.agciSignal: PRICE_DISCIPLINE / GREED COOLER / VALUATION MORE EXTREME

items.headline: Google commits at least EUR 13 billion to Finnish AI infrastructure with long-term power supply
items.summary: Google said it will invest at least EUR 13 billion in AI infrastructure in Finland over two years, alongside a long-term power purchase agreement with Fortum. The announcement links AI compute expansion directly to contracted electricity rather than headline data-center capacity alone.
items.whyItMatters: This is positive evidence for the AGCI AI quality framework: funded capex plus contracted power improves credibility of demand. It also reinforces electricity generation and grid access as binding strategic assets in AI infrastructure.
items.agciSignal: AI CAPEX + CONTRACTED POWER / HIGHER QUALITY DEMAND SIGNAL

items.headline: China producer inflation accelerates as energy costs feed through
items.summary: Official Chinese data showed August PPI rising 3.8% year over year, above the 3.6% consensus and July's 3.5%, while CPI rose 0.8%. Reuters linked the acceleration partly to elevated energy costs and Middle East supply risks.
items.whyItMatters: The energy shock is broadening geographically. A stronger producer-price impulse in China reduces the disinflationary cushion that global goods prices previously provided and raises the hurdle rate for duration and long-multiple assets.
items.agciSignal: GLOBAL ENERGY INFLATION BROADENING / DISINFLATION CUSHION WEAKER

items.headline: AI risk and energy constraints remain central as oil reaches USD 100
items.summary: Barron's morning edition frames oil at USD 100 and AI-related market risk as the key issues for the session. Its emphasis is directionally consistent with the AGCI view that AI opportunity remains large but increasingly dependent on power availability, financing quality and valuation discipline.
items.whyItMatters: The newsletter reinforces, rather than changes, AGCI's selective AI posture. Incremental exposure should favor funded projects with visible power, utilization, margin conversion and free cash flow.
items.agciSignal: AI SELECTIVITY + ENERGY CONSTRAINTS / NO BROAD MULTIPLE CHASE
